info.title: GroundTruth
info.description: Independent causal verification for climate restoration and carbon-credit claims. This API returns evidence bundles with full provenance, not bare scores. A divergence between an independent estimate and a developer claim is a trigger for accredited review, never a finding of fraud.

get.description:
Runs matching the filters, newest first, in pages.

Pagination is by cursor, not offset: the sort key (`created_at`, `run_id`) never
changes, so runs written while you page cannot shift or repeat a page. A run whose
write commits late can be missing from the scroll in progress and appears in the
next one. There is no total count; it would be stale as soon as it was read.

get.summary: Compare two runs by evidence id
get.description:
A per-evidence-id diff: each id is `added`, `removed`, `changed` or `unchanged`.

**NOT COMPARABLE.** When the runs are for different cases, differ in data mode or
engine version, were written under incompatible contracts, or one has no evidence
bundle (refused, failed, queued, cancelled), the response says `comparable: false`
with every reason and returns **no diff**. A difference across engine versions is
not presented as a change. Runs from different specifications are comparable, with
`same_specification: false`.

get.description:
One run with its outcome and, when it has one, its evidence bundle.

A refused run returns `200` with `result_state: "refused"` and the structured
error (code, stage, message, remediation, detail). A run still queued or running
returns its state with no bundle.

With `include_report=true` a run that has a bundle also carries `report_markdown`,
rendered on read by the deterministic renderer. No language model narrates a
stored run.

post.description:
Queue a simulated analysis for a case and return at once; poll `status_url`.

* **`202`**: a new job was queued.
* **`200`**: nothing new was queued. Either a stored result already answers this exact
  request (`from_cache`), or an identical job is already in flight (`deduplicated`).
  `run_id` is that existing run.

Only simulated data can run, and the response says so (`is_simulated`, `notice`).
`synthetic: false` is refused with `501`; it is never quietly simulated. There is no
`true_effect` field: it is not part of the specification hash, so accepting it would
let two different simulations share one cached answer.

200.description: An existing result or job answers it.

503.description: The job store is not available.

get.description:
Where a job is, cheap enough to poll about once a second until `terminal` is true.

`stages` are what was observed as the job moved through the worker: claim, data access,
the engine, recording. The engine is one uninterruptible step, so its internal timings
(`engine_metrics`) appear only after it finishes, and there is **no percentage** at any
point. While the engine runs you get its `elapsed_ms`, which is time spent, not
progress. A **refusal** is `succeeded` with `result_state: "refused"`: the job worked.

503.description: The job store is not available.

post.description:
Stop a job.

* **queued** → `200`, `cancelled` at once; no worker will start it.
* **running** → `202`, still `running` with `cancel_requested: true`. The engine is one
  uninterruptible step, so the worker honours the request when it reaches a checkpoint
  or the engine returns; the result is then discarded and the job ends `cancelled`.
* **already cancelled**, or cancel already requested → the same answer again.
* **succeeded or failed** → `409 job_already_finished`; nothing changes.

202.description: Running: cancel requested, not yet honoured.

503.description: The job store is not available.

get.description:
Emit a `progress` event with the full job view on every change, then a final `done`.

The stream ends once the job is terminal. Unknown jobs are `404` and an unavailable
store is `503` before any event is sent, exactly as for `GET /jobs/{run_id}`.

503.description: The job store is not available.

Run the verification pipeline for a case.

Synchronous today. The analysis job lifecycle (queue, poll, cancel) is
tracked separately; this endpoint keeps the same response shape so the
frontend contract does not change when it moves behind a job.

422.description: Either the request body is invalid (a validation error), or the engine refused or rejected the request (an engine failure, where `is_refusal` says which). A refusal is a legitimate outcome, not a malfunction.

501.description: Not implemented: observed data (a plain message), or a capability the engine does not have (an engine failure).

503.description: A required dataset could not be retrieved.

Confidence.title: Confidence
Confidence.description:
An interval estimate with an explicit interpretation.

``kind`` records whether the interval is a classical confidence interval, a
permutation-based range, or a sensitivity envelope. Reporting these as if
they were interchangeable would be misleading.

CreateCaseRequest.title: CreateCaseRequest
CreateCaseRequest.description: Request to define and register a new project case.

version.title: Version
version.description: Provider version or snapshot date, e.g. '2024.1'.

retrieved_at.title: Retrieved At
retrieved_at.description: ISO timestamp of retrieval, set by the platform.

DatasetRef.title: DatasetRef
DatasetRef.description:
A pinned reference to an external dataset.

The platform resolves a logical dataset name to a concrete, versioned
reference before the engine runs. The engine never chooses a dataset
version, so a re-run months later uses the same imagery rather than
whatever the provider currently serves.

DiffSummary.title: DiffSummary
DiffSummary.description: How many ids fall in each status.

EngineFailureBody.title: EngineFailureBody
EngineFailureBody.description: The body ``/verify`` returns when the engine refused or could not run.

EngineFailureDetail.title: EngineFailureDetail
EngineFailureDetail.description:
Why ``/verify`` returned no result: the engine refused, or could not run.

``is_refusal`` is the field that matters. A refusal is the system correctly declining
to produce a fragile number, and is shown as a legitimate outcome, not as an error.

stages.title: Stages
stages.description: The engine's internal stages and how long each took, in order. The engine reports these only for a completed analysis; a refusal or error has none.

stopped_at.title: Stopped At
stopped_at.description: The stage a refusal or error came from, as the engine names it.

EngineMetricsView.title: EngineMetricsView
EngineMetricsView.description: The engine's own timings, taken from ``RunMetrics``. Present only after it returns.

ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode
ErrorCode.description:
Machine-readable failure reasons.

The API maps these to HTTP status codes and the UI maps them to copy, so
neither has to parse an error message. Adding a member is a minor contract
change; changing what one means is a major one.

label.title: Label
label.description: Short human-readable description of the quantity.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: Unit from the declared vocabulary, or '' if none.

Evidence.title: Evidence
Evidence.description: One auditable value with its unit, uncertainty and origin.

EvidenceBundle.title: EvidenceBundle
EvidenceBundle.description:
An immutable, verified collection of evidence for one case.

The bundle is the hand-off point from the deterministic pipeline to the
reporting layer. It is serialisable, diffable and fully reproducible from
its provenance records.

EvidenceSnapshot.title: EvidenceSnapshot
EvidenceSnapshot.description: An evidence item as one side of the diff saw it.

FieldChange.title: FieldChange
FieldChange.description: One field of one evidence item that differs.

engine_capabilities.title: Engine Capabilities
engine_capabilities.description: What the engine can actually do, reported by the engine itself.

earth_observation_implemented.description: False until the Earth Engine reducer chain lands.

genai_narration_implemented.title: Genai Narration Implemented

ItemDiff.description: One evidence id across the two bundles.

from_cache.description: An existing result answers this request; nothing was queued or will run.

deduplicated.title: Deduplicated
deduplicated.description: An identical job is already queued or running; this is that job.

JobSubmission.title: JobSubmission
JobSubmission.description: What submitting did: queued a new job, or pointed at an existing run.

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.description: True once nothing more will happen; stop polling.

attempt.title: Attempt
attempt.description: How many times a worker has taken the job.

cancel_requested.title: Cancel Requested
cancel_requested.description: True once a cancel was requested. A running job honours it when its worker reaches a checkpoint or the engine returns.

stage.title: Stage
stage.description: The live stage in progress, if one is recorded.

last_heartbeat_at.title: Last Heartbeat At
last_heartbeat_at.description: When the worker last renewed its lease. Coarse: about a third of the lease.

retry_at.title: Retry At
retry_at.description: When a job waiting to retry becomes available again.

error.description: A refusal (is_refusal true) or an engine error, once recorded.

result_url.title: Result Url
result_url.description: Where the stored result is, once there is one.

note.title: Note
note.default: There is no percentage because none can be known: the analysis engine runs as one step and reports its internal timings only when it finishes. `stages` are observed as they happen; `engine_metrics` fills in afterwards.

JobView.title: JobView
JobView.description:
A job's status and progress, small enough to poll every second.

A **refusal** is a completed job: ``status`` is ``succeeded``, ``result_state`` is
``refused``, ``terminal`` is true and ``error.is_refusal`` is true. It is never
``failed``. ``is_simulated`` and ``data_mode`` are always present, and a simulated job
carries a ``notice``.

MessageErrorBody.title: MessageErrorBody
MessageErrorBody.description: An error whose ``detail`` is a plain message, e.g. an unknown case (404).

NotComparable.title: NotComparable
NotComparable.description: One reason two runs cannot be compared.

source.title: Source
source.description: Data source or upstream system, e.g. 'Sentinel-2 L2A'.

method.title: Method
method.description: Algorithm or estimator that produced the value.

source_uri.title: Source Uri
source_uri.description: Resolvable identifier for the source (URL, asset id, DOI).

retrieved_at.title: Retrieved At
retrieved_at.description: When the underlying data was retrieved.

code_version.title: Code Version
code_version.description: Git SHA or package version of the producing code.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: Estimator parameters needed to reproduce the value.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: Evidence ids this value was derived from.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Caveats a human auditor should read.

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description:
An immutable record of the origin of a single analytical value.

Every :class:`~groundtruth.contracts.evidence.Evidence` item must carry one.
Without provenance a number cannot be audited, and an un-auditable number is
not admissible in a verification report.

not_comparable.title: Not Comparable
not_comparable.description: Every reason the pair cannot be compared; empty when comparable.

same_specification.title: Same Specification
same_specification.description: False when the two runs were requested with different specifications (inputs, window, seed, or pinned datasets). Still comparable; read the diff knowing it.

RunComparison.title: RunComparison
RunComparison.description:
Two runs compared by evidence id, or the reasons they cannot be.

``comparable: false`` means NOT COMPARABLE: ``diff`` is null and no difference is
presented, because across engine versions, data modes or cases a difference in a
number may be an artefact of the instrument and not a change in the project.

RunItem.title: RunItem
RunItem.description:
One stored run, as a list or a comparison shows it.

``status`` is the job; ``result_state`` is what happened to the analysis, in the
UI's existing vocabulary. A **refused** run is a successful job (``status`` is
``succeeded``) whose ``result_state`` is ``refused``: a legitimate outcome to
display, never an error. ``is_simulated`` and ``data_mode`` are always present.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. Null on the last page.

contains_simulated.title: Contains Simulated
contains_simulated.description: True if any run on this page is simulated.

RunListPage.title: RunListPage
RunListPage.description: A page of runs, newest first.

RunMetrics.title: RunMetrics
RunMetrics.description: Timings and counters, for monitoring and capacity planning.

state.title: State
state.description: done | active | pending | skipped (never reached) | failed | unknown (no stage was recorded for this job).

elapsed_ms.title: Elapsed Ms
elapsed_ms.description: Time spent in the active stage so far. A clock reading, not a fraction of anything.

StageView.title: StageView
StageView.description: One live stage of a job, as it was observed.

synthetic.title: Synthetic
synthetic.description: Must be true until real Earth-observation providers are implemented. false is refused with 501, never silently simulated.

SubmitJobRequest.title: SubmitJobRequest
SubmitJobRequest.description: Queue an analysis for a case. Simulated data only, until real providers exist.

VerdictDiff.title: VerdictDiff
VerdictDiff.description:
The screening verdicts side by side. Neutral by construction: it states the
two labels and whether they differ, and ranks neither.

VerdictLabel.title: VerdictLabel
VerdictLabel.description: Screening outcomes. None of these is a finding of fraud.

synthetic.title: Synthetic
synthetic.description: Must be true until real Earth-observation providers are implemented. A request with synthetic=false is rejected rather than silently simulated.

true_effect.title: True Effect
true_effect.description: Effect injected into the simulated treated unit.

spec_hash.title: Spec Hash
spec_hash.description: Hash of the analysis specification. Identical hashes must yield identical results under the same engine version.

VerificationResponse.title: VerificationResponse
VerificationResponse.description: The result of a verification run.

divergence_ratio.title: Divergence Ratio
divergence_ratio.description: Independent estimate / claimed effect, where both are commensurable.

caveats.title: Caveats
default: A divergence between an independent estimate and a developer claim is not evidence of fraud; it indicates that the claim warrants accredited review.
Spectral indices track vegetation condition, not carbon stocks.
Estimates are conditional on the donor pool and the pre-treatment fit reported alongside them.

VerificationVerdict.title: VerificationVerdict
VerificationVerdict.description: The screening conclusion, phrased so it cannot be read as an accusation.

WarningsDiff.title: WarningsDiff
WarningsDiff.description: Analyst-facing warnings that appear in only one bundle.
